children: Shares of cloud computing and online retail behemoth Amazon
jumped 4.8% in the morning session after JPMorgan named the company a top artificial intelligence pick on its Analyst Focus List, citing accelerating long-term growth across Amazon Web Services.

JPMorgan analyst Doug Anmuth pointed to cloud momentum as the primary catalyst, observing in a client note reported by CNBC that Amazon expects AWS revenue growth of more than 40% in both 2027 and 2028, with the unit on track to reach $1 trillion in annual revenue over the next five to ten years alongside improving capital return visibility.

Contributing to the momentum, the major indices rebounded with the tech heavy Nasdaq index up more than 2% in the morning session as dip buyers stepped in following a severe rout driven by artificial intelligence names in the previous week.
After the initial pop, the shares cooled down to $269.47, up 4% from the previous close.
What is the market telling us

Amazon’s shares are not very volatile and have only had 4 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful, although it might not be something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 5 days ago when the stock gained 7.7% on the news that U.S. midterm election results delivered a Democratic sweep of Congress easing political uncertainty and pulling Treasury yields lower following weeks of sector selling.

Also, investors are betting that regulatory curbs on new data centers would slow runaway capital spending and enhance the value of existing infrastructure. Tighter construction timelines also protect incumbent pricing power. In an analysis by CNBC, market strategists observed that with cloud demand exceeding supply, permitting restrictions prevent an oversupply glut and increase the value of operational sites.

Amazon is up 19% since the beginning of the year, and at $269.47 per share, it is trading close to its 52-week high of $284.02 from August 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of Amazon’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $1,507.
